text:
Ibrahim Khan: seeing more noise around streaming edge cases again. We need to lock semantics for partial SSE frames + proxy buffering + mid-stream disconnects. Also: do we ever attempt reconnect automatically? Trying to keep consistent across py/ts/go.

I dropped quick notes in the scratchpad: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rwi-redwood-streaming-edge-cases ("streaming-edge-cases-notes")

Top cases:
1) partial frames (event boundaries split across TCP reads)
2) proxy buffering (no chunks for ~30-60s, then burst)
3) server disconnect after some tokens (customer sees `socket hang up` / `unexpected EOF`)

Dana Lo: +1. In TS we’ve seen (1) + (3) a lot, esp behind corporate proxies. In Node/undici we sometimes get data chunks that cut right through `\n\n` boundaries. Our current parser assumes we get full lines most of the time :grimacing:

Owen Phillips: from Support side, repro from a customer is basically: Cloudflare in front + enterprise proxy. They see a few tokens, then nothing, then disconnect. We have logs w/ request-id showing gateway still streaming but client times out / proxy buffers. SUP thread has similar symptoms.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go reader has a similar issue if we rely on bufio.Scanner default token size. It also breaks on long lines if we ever get a huge `data:` line (like tool output). We should not use Scanner defaults here.

Sabrina James: for docs/examples, we should be explicit: “don’t parse SSE by splitting on chunk boundaries” and show robust parser patterns.

Amara Diallo: from gateway perspective: we do send `text/event-stream`, and we flush as we write tokens. But intermediaries can buffer; we can’t guarantee flush reaches client immediately. We can guarantee event format though: `data: ...\n\n` with occasional `event:` types.

Rafael Mendes: reconnect question: we should be *very* careful. If we retry a streaming request after partial output, we might duplicate tokens or produce different output. Unless requests are explicitly resumable / idempotent (they aren’t today). Default should be: no automatic reconnect once body streaming began.

Ibrahim Khan: agree. I’m leaning:
- if connection fails *before* we receive any SSE events (no `data:` yet), can treat as safe to retry (like non-streaming) subject to retry budget.
- if we got at least one event, surface error + let app decide.

Dana Lo: how do we detect “received any events” consistently? In TS we can set a boolean when we parse first full event (not just first bytes). But if we get partial bytes and then disconnect, we might have received some of the first event but not parse it.

Mateusz Zielinski: for Go, we can track when we successfully parse an event delimiter (`\n\n`) and have at least one `data:` field. If disconnect happens mid-frame, that counts as “started streaming” IMO because server might have generated tokens.

Rafael Mendes: yep. From SRE angle, being conservative is safer: if you get *any* response body bytes after headers, treat it as started. Otherwise you risk duplicate work and customer confusion.

Amara Diallo: +1. Also worth noting: some proxies will deliver headers immediately but buffer body. So you might see headers, then nothing for 30s, then burst. If SDK treats “no tokens yet” as “safe to retry”, we’ll create retry storms on long first-token latencies.

Ibrahim Khan: good point. So distinction should be “have we received any body bytes” not “parsed an event”.

Wei Chen: can we capture this in the standard doc w/ user guidance like: if you need resume semantics, use non-streaming + polling / or provide your own idempotency key? (Even if we don’t support resumable stream yet.)

Dana Lo: concrete TS parser fix:
- accumulate bytes into buffer
- parse lines by `\n` (but handle `\r\n` too)
- build event until blank line
- allow `data:` lines repeated; concatenate w/ `\n` per SSE spec
- ignore comments `:`

We should add tests for:
- `da` + `ta: {..}\n\n` split across chunks
- `data:` split such that newline arrives later

Mateusz Zielinski: same in Go; avoid Scanner, use bufio.Reader and `ReadString('\n')` or manual state machine. Also handle long lines; tool call args can be big.

Owen Phillips: for proxy buffering: customers think we hung. If we set a super low “read timeout” for streaming, we’ll falsely error. Current SDK defaults vary (TS has ~30s idle timeout in some envs). Need to align.

Rafael Mendes: streaming timeouts: recommended is either disabled idle read timeout or very high (like 5m) but keep an overall deadline configurable. Otherwise any proxy hiccup = customer pain.

Ibrahim Khan: so for the standard:
- Streaming requests: no per-chunk/idle read timeout by default (or set to something generous like 5m), overall timeout default maybe 10m? (needs review)
- Non-streaming: shorter overall + connect/read defaults.

Dana Lo: reconnect semantics proposal (TS):
- if network error occurs before we read first byte of body -> eligible for retry (same policy as non-streaming)
- if after first body byte -> surface `StreamDisconnectedError` with metadata (bytes_received, events_received if known) and include request-id if we have it

Mateusz Zielinski: +1, in Go we can include wrapped errors: `context canceled` should remain distinct from `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`.

Amara Diallo: request-id: we set `x-request-id` in headers. If SDK starts reading body, it should still have captured headers. Please make sure the error includes request-id consistently.

Sabrina James: for examples: show cancellation best practices too. For TS: `AbortController.abort()`; for Go: context cancel; for Python: close response iterator.

Ibrahim Khan: action items:
- I’ll add a section to ADR-0138 draft: “no automatic reconnect after any body bytes” + rationale (duplicates / proxy buffering / retry storms).
- Dana/Mateusz: add conformance cases for partial frame parsing + mid-frame disconnect -> deterministic error classification.
- Owen: drop the strongest repro steps + any sanitized logs into the scratchpad doc so we can reference in PRs.

Dana Lo: ack. I’ll also check how undici handles `ReadableStream` backpressure; we might need to ensure we don’t buffer entire response.

Rafael Mendes: please also include guidance for metrics: count `stream_disconnect_after_body_bytes` separately from `connect_failures` so we can detect if a release changes behavior.

Ibrahim Khan: noted. Adding to telemetry hooks list.

Owen Phillips: adding support ticket link here (internal): https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-9321 (similar symptoms) and another TS one where parsing blew up on partial frames. Will sanitize details.

Wei Chen: when you have a stable decision, ping Docs thread; we’ll update streaming troubleshooting section with “proxy buffering is normal; increase overall timeout; don’t assume 30s idle == hung”.

Ibrahim Khan: will do. :thumbsup:
